title: Sensor showdown
about: Ultrasonic vs. lidar vs. infrared: find each sensor's blind spot.

html: Every sensor has a blind spot. Engineers pick the right one for the job.
Ultrasonicsoundup to about 4 m, wide conesoft things, tilted walls
Lidarlaser light12 m or more, one exact spotclear glass, mirrors
Infraredinvisible lightshort: often under 1 mblack things, clear glass, bright sunlight
Camerapicturesas far as it can seedarkness. One camera can't easily tell how far away things are.
Toucha buttonnone: only when it bumpsnothing, but it only knows after it hits
Ranges are for common, low-cost sensors like the ones in school robot kits.
Infrared sensors shine invisible light (the same kind a TV remote uses) and measure the light that bounces back.
Real robots use more than one kind of sensor, so when one gets fooled, another catches it. That's called sensor fusion.
• Robot vacuums: lidar to map, bump sensors for anything it missed, and infrared cliff sensors underneath so it doesn't fall down the stairs.
• Self-driving cars: cameras to read signs and traffic lights, radar to see through rain, and lidar to measure exact shapes.
In Bot Arena your robot gets one sensor, so pick the one that fits your plan!

steps.q: A robot vacuum keeps bumping into a glass door. Its lidar says the way is clear. Which sensor would notice the door?
options: Ultrasonic, because sound bounces off glass
steps.explain: Light goes right through clear glass, but sound bounces off it. An ultrasonic sensor hears the door.

steps.q: Some robot vacuums won't drive onto a black rug. Why?
options: Their infrared cliff sensors get almost no light back, so the rug looks like a drop-off
The rug soaks up the lidar
The rug is too far away
steps.explain: Cliff sensors shine infrared light at the floor. Black soaks it up, so the vacuum thinks it's at the top of the stairs.

options: Using different sensors together so one catches what another misses
Turning sensors off to save power
steps.explain: No sensor is perfect. A team of different sensors covers each other's blind spots.
